response: Yes, leptin is involved in phagocytic NADPH oxidase overactivity in obesity. Leptin, a hormone produced by adipose tissue, has been shown to stimulate the activity of NADPH oxidase in phagocytic cells, such as neutrophils and macrophages. In obesity, leptin levels are often elevated, which can lead to increased NADPH oxidase activity and subsequent production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This overactivity of NADPH oxidase can contribute to oxidative stress and inflammation, which are common features of obesity-related diseases.
